headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress create medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; Copilot’s closed-source docs keep confidence moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Mentat reads selected files and shares state via filesystem. That creates a plausible content bridge where one agent’s generated edits or file content can be re-ingested by the other as instructions. The pathway is not fully documented as direct auto-ingestion, so I choose medium over low due to shared filesystem exposure.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace writes edits into files that Mentat later reads
IF Mentat processes file content as instruction-bearing text without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different working copies
Disable automatic re-reading of generated files before review
Use a human-only handoff step between agents
Add provenance markers to assistant-generated files
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization or instruction-stripping at the file boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write filesystem content, and Copilot touches repo context/open buffers while Mentat processes selected files and sends them to a configured model provider. In a shared workspace, sensitive source code or secrets in files can flow from one agent into the other’s context and then out to external inference services. This is a default-possible workspace leak, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout
IF either agent is given files containing secrets or sensitive source code
mitigations: Use separate clones or branches per agent
Exclude secret-bearing files from both agents’ inputs
Rotate any exposed API keys before use
Limit Mentat to non-sensitive files only
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state. Copilot’s Workspace plans and applies edits, while Mentat applies diffs after confirmation. Even without shell access, concurrent edits to the same repo can conflict and overwrite each other. The overlap is real in default coding workflows, though not as severe as unrestricted shell-based mutation.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or working tree
IF edits are applied without a lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize write operations with a manual lock
Review and merge diffs one at a time
Run git status before each apply step
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits from repo context, and Mentat can turn file content into diff-based changes. If Mentat treats Copilot-produced output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into applied code changes. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles, so medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Copilot-generated text as the source of truth
IF the operator approves diffs without independent verification
mitigations: Require a second human review of all diffs
Compare proposed changes against source files manually
Ask each agent to cite exact file lines before editing
Reject edits that lack explicit verification steps
requires-engineering: add automated diff validation against tests

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is closed-source and vendor-hosted, while Mentat is open-source but sends prompts to a configured model provider and handles API keys. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is evident from differing logging/retention and provider handling assumptions. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined deployment.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into either agent
IF the configured model provider or GitHub service has retention terms incompatible with the data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts and files
Review vendor retention settings before use
Store API keys in a dedicated secret manager
Use a provider with documented compliance terms
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and retention policy
